2816:     )
2817: 
2818:     l1 = s1.shape[0]
2819:     l2 = s2.shape[0]
2820: 
2821:     if be.is_numpy:
2822:         acc_cost_mat = njit_lcss_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, eps, mask)
2823:     else:
2824:         acc_cost_mat = lcss_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, eps, mask, be=be)
2825:     path = _return_lcss_path(s1, s2, eps, mask, acc_cost_mat, l1, l2, be=be)
2826: 
2827:     return path, float(acc_cost_mat[-1][-1]) / min([l1, l2])
2828: 
2829: 
2830: @njit()
2831: def njit_lcss_accumulated_matrix_from_dist_matrix(dist_matrix, eps, mask):
2832:     """Compute the accumulated cost matrix score between two time series using
2833:     a precomputed distance matrix.
2834: 
2835:     Parameters
2836:     ----------
2837:     dist_matrix : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2838:         Array containing the pairwise distances.
2839:     eps : float (default: 1.)
2840:         Maximum matching distance threshold.
2841:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2842:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
2843: 
2844:     Returns
2845:     -------
2846:     acc_cost_mat : array-like, shape=(sz1 + 1, sz2 + 1)
2847:         Accumulated cost matrix.
2848:     """
2849:     l1, l2 = dist_matrix.shape
2850:     acc_cost_mat = numpy.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), 0)
2851: 
2852:     for i in range(1, l1 + 1):
2853:         for j in range(1, l2 + 1):
2854:             if numpy.isfinite(mask[i - 1, j - 1]):
2855:                 if dist_matrix[i - 1, j - 1] <= eps:
2856:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = 1 + acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j - 1]
2857:                 else:
2858:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = max(
2859:                         acc_cost_mat[i][j - 1], acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j]
2860:                     )
2861: 
2862:     return acc_cost_mat
2863: 
2864: 
2865: def lcss_accumulated_matrix_from_dist_matrix(dist_matrix, eps, mask, be=None):
2866:     """Compute the accumulated cost matrix score between two time series using
2867:     a precomputed distance matrix.
2868: 
2869:     Parameters
2870:     ----------
2871:     dist_matrix : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2872:         Array containing the pairwise distances.
2873:     eps : float (default: 1.)
2874:         Maximum matching distance threshold.
2875:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2876:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
2877:     be : Backend object or string or None
2878:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
2879:         the NumPy backend is used.
2880:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
2881:         the PyTorch backend is used.
2882:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
2883:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
2884: 
2885:     Returns
2886:     -------
2887:     acc_cost_mat : array-like, shape=(sz1 + 1, sz2 + 1)
2888:         Accumulated cost matrix.
2889:     """
2890:     be = instantiate_backend(be, dist_matrix)
2891:     dist_matrix = be.array(dist_matrix)
2892:     l1, l2 = be.shape(dist_matrix)
2893:     acc_cost_mat = be.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), 0)
2894: 
2895:     for i in range(1, l1 + 1):
2896:         for j in range(1, l2 + 1):
2897:             if mask[i - 1, j - 1]:
2898:                 if dist_matrix[i - 1, j - 1] <= eps:
2899:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = 1 + acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j - 1]
2900:                 else:
2901:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = max(
2902:                         acc_cost_mat[i][j - 1], acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j]
2903:                     )
2904: 
2905:     return acc_cost_mat
2906: 
2907: 
2908: def lcss_path_from_metric(
2909:     s1,
2910:     s2=None,
2911:     eps=1,
2912:     metric="euclidean",
2913:     global_constraint=None,
2914:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
2915:     itakura_max_slope=None,
2916:     be=None,
2917:     **kwds
2918: ):
2919:     r"""Compute the Longest Common Subsequence (LCSS) similarity measure between
2920:     (possibly multidimensional) time series using a distance metric defined by
2921:     the user and return both the path and the similarity.
2922: 
2923:     Having the length of the longest commom subsequence between two time series,
2924:     the similarity is computed as the percentage of that value regarding the
2925:     length of the shortest time series.
2926: 
2927:     It is not required that both time series share the same size, but they must
2928:     be the same dimension. LCSS was originally presented in [1]_.
2929: 
2930:     Valid values for metric are the same as for scikit-learn
2931:     `pairwise_distances`_ function i.e. a string (e.g. "euclidean",
2932:     "sqeuclidean", "hamming") or a function that is used to compute the
2933:     pairwise distances. See `scikit`_ and `scipy`_ documentations for more
2934:     information about the available metrics.
2935: 
2936:     Parameters
2937:     ----------
2938:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,) if metric!="precomputed", (sz1, sz2) otherwise
2939:         A time series or an array of pairwise distances between samples.
2940:         If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2941:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,), optional (default: None)
2942:         A second time series, only allowed if metric != "precomputed".
2943:         If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2944:     eps : float (default: 1.)
2945:         Maximum matching distance threshold.
2946:     metric : string or callable (default: "euclidean")
2947:         Function used to compute the pairwise distances between each points of
2948:         `s1` and `s2`.
2949:         If metric is "precomputed", `s1` is assumed to be a distance matrix.
2950:         If metric is an other string, it must be one of the options compatible
2951:         with sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances.
2952:         Alternatively, if metric is a callable function, it is called on pairs
2953:         of rows of `s1` and `s2`. The callable should take two 1 dimensional
2954:         arrays as input and return a value indicating the distance between
2955:         them.
2956:     global_constraint : {"itakura", "sakoe_chiba"} or None (default: None)
2957:         Global constraint to restrict admissible paths for LCSS.
2958:     sakoe_chiba_radius : int or None (default: None)
2959:         Radius to be used for Sakoe-Chiba band global constraint.
2960:         The Sakoe-Chiba radius corresponds to the parameter :math:`\delta` mentioned in [1]_,
2961:         it controls how far in time we can go in order to match a given
2962:         point from one time series to a point in another time series.
2963:         If None and `global_constraint` is set to "sakoe_chiba", a radius of
2964:         1 is used.
2965:         If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
2966:         `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
2967:         two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
2968:         constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
2969:         used.
2970:     itakura_max_slope : float or None (default: None)
2971:         Maximum slope for the Itakura parallelogram constraint.
